## Description

A suctorian ciliate living inside a triangular lorica (25–200 × 25–80 µm) on a stalk, with two
bundles of 10–20 tentacles up to 80 µm long that catch passing ciliates and suck out their
cytoplasm. Adults have no cilia; the swarmer (30–35 µm) swims with cilia and then attaches.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `pond` (weight 0.15), `puddle` (weight 0.15); 1 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

Sessile on a short, thick rigid stalk. Prey that touch the tentacles are held (`Captured`) and their
biomass is drained in biological time. Width estimated.

## Not implemented yet

- The tentacles are a reach, not individual capitate tentacles with haptocysts.
- The lorica is not a separate structure; the triangular shape is approximated.
- Reproduction by internal budding of a ciliated swarmer is simplified.

## Unique and shared mechanics

Shares [tentacle feeding](../../mechanics/feeding-and-phagocytosis.md) with *Podophrya* and *Tokophrya*, and the
[rigid stalk](../../mechanics/stalks-and-colonies.md) with *Epistylis*.
